variable_coverage.construction: 1 for a manipulation firm-year with an SEC-accused annual financial-statement manipulation and 0 for a matched control firm-year. Requires the annual event/fiscal-year roster, issuer linkage and exact regression sample/matched sets.

CFO ONEPCT divided by ONEPCT + CFO salary + bonus. ONEPCT is the stock/option portfolio-value change for a 1% stock-price change using the cited Core and Guay method; requires the CFO-year portfolio, option holdings/pricing inputs and salary/bonus data.
CEO ONEPCT divided by ONEPCT + CEO salary + bonus; construct the CEO-year stock/option portfolio sensitivity using the cited method and annual pay inputs.

CEO total compensation divided by the adjusted total compensation of the top five executives, including salary, bonus, other annual compensation, restricted-stock grant value, Black-Scholes option grant value, LTIP and all other compensation. Fill fewer-than-five disclosures using lowest-paid disclosed compensation, and retain top five if more are reported.
Indicator from annual company proxy/10-K evidence that the CEO is also Chairman; field does not appear as a directly verified target measure in the local table.
Indicator from company proxy/10-K evidence that the CEO is a company founder.

Annual percentage change in cash sales, with cash sales = Sales (legacy DATA 12) − annual change in Receivables (legacy DATA 2). The inner annual receivables change nested inside the outer annual percentage change extends raw Compustat needs to t−2.

Annual change in Earnings (legacy DATA 18) / average total assets. Annual change of a scaled measure plus the prior-period average-assets denominator extends raw history to t−2, subject to unverified current-field and denominator mapping.
Annual change in Inventory (legacy DATA 3) / average total assets; needs prior fiscal-year inventory and the corresponding average-assets endpoints.
Annual change in Receivables (legacy DATA 2) / average total assets; needs prior fiscal-year receivables and the corresponding average-assets endpoints.

(ΔWC + ΔNCO + ΔFIN) / average total assets using legacy Compustat DATA components listed in the source. The source does not specify component-change period or average-assets interval, so exact raw lookback is unresolved.

design_coverage.reason: The source specifies conditional likelihood on matched sets and does not report a separate fixed-effect family for the selected fit. Matched-set structure is captured under estimation.
No weighting scheme or weight variable is specified for the selected conditional-logit fit.

implementation_issues.description: Table 4 Panel A column (4) reports 286 observations, while Table 1 reports 116 manipulation plus 219 control firm-years (335 rows); the paper supplies no regression-specific exclusion/count bridge or exact row roster.

The paper reports AAER issuance dates in 1982–2005 but the fit is indexed by annual manipulation firm-years. It excludes firms without a specific manipulation period and annual-only screens; the actual event-year roster and release-to-fiscal-year mapping are not reported. Calendar release years cannot be used as fiscal-year bounds.

Sample construction permits up to two nearest-asset controls per manipulation firm-year, while the conditional-logit explanation says one manipulation firm in each matched pair. Exact matched-set membership, strata IDs, and how this structure yields N=286 are not given.

Compustat legacy DATA numbers are listed but not mapped to current annual fields. The nested cash-sales and scaled-earnings changes require raw t−2 history; RSST component-change and average-assets intervals are not specified.
The source states 1st/99th percentile winsorization but does not say which population determines thresholds or the exact ordering relative to complete-case and matching screens.

Historical issuer/event-to-CUSIP/GVKEY/ExecID and CEO/CFO role links must align the AAER firm, manipulated fiscal year, Compustat year and ExecuComp executive year. Candidate keys and an historical CIK–GVKEY table are present, but sample coverage, validity windows and row-level link chain are unconfirmed.

CEO Chairman and founder indicators are hand-collected from proxy statements or 10-K filings for manipulation and matched firms. The source gives the definitions and document types, but the required issuer/year filing roster and coding evidence must be assembled.

CEO_PAYSLICE requires top-five compensation rank and the paper’s stated adjustment when fewer than five executives are disclosed; the categories must be aligned to annual ExecuComp fields or manually coded proxy values.

CFO/CEO ONEPCT must be reconstructed from fiscal-year-end holdings and option/pricing information following Core and Guay (2002). The article identifies the method; local current-field correspondence and option-pricing settings remain to be checked against that source.

Current ExecuComp includes multiple annual total-compensation definitions and stock/option award fields, while the target defines a specific top-five bundle including Black-Scholes option grant value and LTIP. Historical field-vintage and proxy-backfill correspondence is not established by the live column probes.

evidence.quote: Our sample begins with 2261 AAERs issued by the SEC from May 17th, 1982 through June 10th, 2005.
evidence.description: The stated calendar dates are AAER release dates; the paper separately constructs manipulation fiscal-year periods from release content.

evidence.quote: We first exclude 219 firms that either were charged for conduct other than accounting manipulations (e.g., bribery, disclosure issues, etc.) or could not be linked to specific manipulation periods.
evidence.description: Annual event-period screen and inability to link firms to specific manipulation periods.

evidence.quote: When data are not available in ExecuComp, we hand-collect compensation data from proxy statements (DEF 14A) filed with the SEC Edgar.
evidence.description: The authors use SEC proxy filings as a hand-collection fallback for executive compensation.

evidence.quote: First, SEC Edgar provides proxy statements only since 1994;
evidence.description: The paper’s footnote identifies the historical lower bound of the proxy source it used.

evidence.quote: For each manipulation firm, we identify firms in ExecuComp in the same industry and with total assets in the range of 80–120 percent of the manipulation firm’s total assets in the year prior to the start of the manipulation period.
evidence.description: Matching uses SIC-based industry and prior-period size; exact matched observations are not listed.

evidence.quote: We follow Frankel et al.’s (2002) SIC-based industry classification scheme.
evidence.description: The target paper cites the classification source but does not reproduce the code ranges in this passage.

evidence.quote: Final sample of total AAER firm-year observations with CEO and CFO compensation data 74 116
evidence.description: Table 1 reports 116 manipulation firm-years in the compensation cohort and 219 control firm-years, which totals 335 rows.

evidence.quote: Annual percentage change in cash sales; cash sales is computed as [Sales (DATA 12) – DReceivables (DATA 2)].
evidence.description: Cash-sales control definition nests receivables change inside an annual percentage change.

evidence.quote: Annual change in [Earnings (DATA 18)/Average total assets].
evidence.description: Earnings control definition is an annual change in a scaled measure.

evidence.quote: RSST_ACCRUALS (DWC+DNCO+DFIN)/Average total assets
evidence.description: The paper lists RSST components and Compustat item codes but does not state change or denominator intervals.

evidence.quote: We first calculate ONEPCT as the total change in value of the executive’s stock and stock option portfolio in response to a one percent change in the stock price using the method described by Core and Guay (2002).
evidence.description: CFO/CEO sensitivity numerator and referenced method.

evidence.quote: We then calculate pay-for-performance sensitivity as ONEPCT/(ONEPCT+Salary+Bonus).
evidence.description: Pay-for-performance sensitivity denominator.

evidence.quote: The first measure is the CEO’s percentage of aggregate top five executives’ total compensation, which includes salary, bonus, other annual pay, the total value of restricted stock granted, the Black-Scholes value of stock options granted, long-term incentive payouts, and all other total compensation (CEO_PAYSLICE).
evidence.description: Pay-slice compensation components.

evidence.quote: If proxy statements disclose more than five executives in a given year, we keep the compensation for the top five executives.
evidence.description: The paper retains the top five if a firm reports more than five executives; if fewer, it fills undisclosed executives at the lowest disclosed compensation.

evidence.quote: We obtain the information on Chairman and founder status from companies’ proxy statements or 10-K filings for both manipulation firms and their match firms.
evidence.description: CEO chairman/founder fields require proxy or 10-K coding for cases and matched firms.

evidence.quote: Our estimates are based on conditional logistic regressions because our data consist of matched pairs.
evidence.description: Selected fit is conditional logistic regression on matched sets.

evidence.quote: the conditional logistic regression models the probability of being a manipulation firm conditional on one of the firms in each pair being a manipulation firm
evidence.description: Conditional likelihood is described using one case per matched pair, while sample selection allows up to two controls for a manipulation firm.

evidence.quote: Because the regressions are estimated based on firm year data and there are multiple observations for some firms, we report estimates based on standard error clustered by firm for the regressions.
evidence.description: Standard errors are clustered by firm.

evidence.quote: Number of total observations 303 294 290 286
evidence.description: Table 4 Panel A column (4) reports N=286. The source gives no bridge from Table 1’s 335 compensation-cohort rows.

evidence.quote: Each of the continuous variables is winsorized at 1% and 99% to mitigate outliers.
evidence.description: The selected fit applies 1st/99th percentile winsorization; the threshold reference population is not stated.
